one_line: Browser-local medical appeal desk that gives agents narrow capabilities while gating sensitive disclosure.
what_it_does: Uses tokenized synthetic claim evidence, deterministic policy checks, consented one-field disclosure, protected drafting, and an auditable ledger for medical appeals.
leverage_rationale: Structured, shared case state and explicit disclosure gates materially outperform generic UI driving for privacy-sensitive appeal work; the agent receives capabilities rather than identity.
leverage_evidence: Seven narrow tools are described for evidence, line items, policy rules, scenarios, disclosure, drafting, and export.
Human and agent share a live case with one-field consent and a fail-closed adversarial demonstration.
Frame sheets show a structured appeal workspace, boundary/visibility states, and checkable defects.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, intentional workflow and substantial UI evidence, but no actual video transcript or final end-to-end runtime proof is supplied.
execution_evidence: Contact sheets show a rendered outpatient imaging appeal with structured metadata, warnings, workflow panels, and later privacy/defect views.
Devpost packaging describes browser-local state, consent, ledger, and tests, but the screenshot itself is promotional packaging.
impact_rationale: People appealing denied medical claims have a concrete high-stakes need for policy/evidence assistance without exposing identity; the privacy-aware workflow credibly addresses it using synthetic claims.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies medical-claim appealers needing help with codes, deadlines, missing evidence, and policy rules.
The product explicitly separates useful capabilities from sensitive identifiers and records disclosure decisions.
creativity_rationale: The capability-not-identity framing, adversarial prompt-injection boundary test, and two-visibility appeal model are a fresh and memorable application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Seeded OCR prompt injection is used as a red-team scenario.
Frames show one letter with two visibility levels and an appeal built around checkable defects.
usability_note: The visible workflow is structured and review-oriented, though the dense agent workspace and small evidence text may raise cognitive load.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; visual evidence is contact sheets and a promotional Devpost image.
Final real-world submission or claim resolution is not shown; data is synthetic.
standouts: Fail-closed prompt-injection demonstration with explicit disclosure consent.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-specific privacy design and unusually concrete high-stakes use case, with meaningful visual workflow evidence despite limited end-to-end proof.

Core provider and verification behavior is described as simulated.
standouts: Human remains in control of sensitive actions.

one_line: Consent-first task board where agents can read, propose, and complete tasks only through visible human approvals.
what_it_does: Exposes session-scoped task-board tools with sharing consent, exact write previews, confirmation dialogs, and fail-closed behavior when WebMCP is unavailable.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central to making task semantics, consent, previews, and shared state explicit; generic clicking would be less reliable and less transparent for these boundaries.
leverage_evidence: Three named tools cover list, propose, and complete operations with separate read/write approvals.
Writes preview exact fields and status transitions; cancellation produces no write.
Frame sheets visibly show the task-board/agent workflow and approval states.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a focused, coherent workflow and recorded native proof claims, though no transcript and no independently verifiable end-to-end result are included.
execution_evidence: Description specifies session consent, revocable sharing, confirmation previews, and fail-closed registration.
Frame sheets show populated task-board states and workflow dialogs.
impact_rationale: Teams and individuals benefit from agent speed without losing authority over task-board data or writes; the value is credible though the scope is intentionally narrow.
impact_evidence: Product addresses trust and authority problems in AI task management.
Visible approval and exact-field previews preserve human control.
creativity_rationale: The explicit separation of read consent, write preview, and write confirmation is a thoughtful interaction model, even though task boards are familiar.

WebMCP unavailable state registers no tools and fails closed.
usability_note: Clear consent and preview boundaries should make agent actions legible and reversible.
red_flags: No transcript and no direct invocation text in the packet.
Scope is a small task board, so impact is bounded.
standouts: Exact-field previews and separate approval gates.
advance_reason: A disciplined, well-evidenced WebMCP collaboration pattern with clear safety semantics and a coherent visible workflow.

one_line: Agent-assisted trades quote intake that turns ordinary-language homeowner requests into validated service-specific briefs.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes domain-level service matching, structured facts, permissions, and validation rather than brittle form clicks; this is a substantial improvement for ambiguous homeowner requests.
leverage_evidence: Tools match unchanged natural-language requests to exact service routes and support semantic recovery.
Two independent jobs remain separate and finalization is permission-gated.

Frames show the service/job brief interface and validation states.

creativity_rationale: Natural-language-to-route matching plus safe semantic fallback and multi-job separation is a fresh, well-pursued angle on quote intake, though the underlying marketplace is familiar.

usability_note: The design emphasizes ordinary-language entry, visible inference, missing gates, and explicit permission, which is well aligned with homeowner needs.
red_flags: Final live lead submission is not performed; success is a server-validated test receipt.

standouts: Strong domain-level WebMCP abstraction over ambiguous service selection.

advance_reason: Strong demonstrated workflow, clear audience value, and a meaningful WebMCP delta in a practical consumer use case.

one_line: WebMCP-enabled Godot-in-the-browser studio for agents to build, test, and iterate on games.
what_it_does: Extends a WebAssembly Godot engine with a custom plugin and WebMCP tools so agents can manipulate game projects and continuously iterate with users.
leverage_rationale: Structured engine access changes the development loop from copying code/screenshots into direct project-state manipulation, testing, and iteration; that is difficult to replicate comparably via generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Godot is compiled to WebAssembly and exposed through custom script/plugin WebMCP tools.
Description explicitly claims agent build, test, and continuous iteration capabilities.
Frame sheets show the browser game-development studio and generated game states.
execution_rationale: The architecture and intended workflow are coherent and frames show a working-looking studio, but the packet does not show a video or a clearly completed generated-game end-to-end result.

Frames show a populated Godot/browser development interface and game output.
No video is submitted and description does not provide concrete test output.
impact_rationale: Beginners and professional developers could benefit from lowering setup and iteration friction, though the claim of fully functional continuous development is only partially evidenced.
impact_evidence: Target audience includes people with little experience and professional game developers.
Packet identifies copy/paste and screenshot-based engine-agent loops as the problem.
creativity_rationale: Directly exposing a game engine's structured state to an agent for creation and iterative testing is an ambitious and memorable use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Custom Godot plugin and WebAssembly engine extension.
Agent can build out requested games and iterate rather than merely invoke UI actions.
usability_note: Potentially powerful, but engine complexity and limited demonstrated end-to-end evidence leave the practical UX uncertain.
red_flags: Built on preexisting Godot engine; novelty is the extension, not the engine itself.
No submitted video or transcript; continuous iteration claims are not fully demonstrated.
advance_reason: High leverage and creativity with a credible technical extension, despite only moderate execution evidence.
